question: In a child with thalassaemia major requiring regular transfusions, the target pre-transfusion haemoglobin should be maintained above 9–10 g/dL to suppress ineffective erythropoiesis and prevent skeletal deformities.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Thalassaemia major requires a hypertransfusion programme targeting pre-transfusion Hb >9–10 g/dL. Allowing Hb to fall lower allows the marrow to try to compensate with ineffective erythropoiesis, causing the characteristic skeletal changes.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The hypertransfusion regimen (maintaining pre-transfusion Hb >9–10 g/dL) suppresses the bone-marrow drive for ineffective erythropoiesis, preventing the characteristic skull bossing, facial deformity, and hepatosplenomegaly that occur with sub-optimal transfusion.
